description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — the gate resolves a constructor callee through its MEMBER CHAIN, so `new globalThis.Response(...)` is recognised identically to a bare `new Response(...)` and fires E-PROTECT-004. Pins the fix for a measured fail-open: the source-text detector this replaced tested `/\bnew\s+Response\b/`, which a member chain does not match, so this exact file compiled at exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics and the emitted handler shipped `{"id":1,"name":"ada","passwordHash":"…"}` to the client. Any aliasing receiver reaches the same conclusion, whether spelled with a dot (`window.Response`, `globalThis.foo.Response`) or with a static-string bracket (`globalThis["Response"]` — see the sibling case `protect-raw-egress-computed-response`, which pins the bracket form after it was measured to evade this detector's first cut). The residual is a callee whose name is not in the tree at all (a dynamic key `globalThis[k]`, or a local rebinding `let R = Response`); that bound is stated in `collectRawEgressFacts` / `detectProtectedRawEgressAcrossFns`, not claimed closed. A key BUILT from literals is NOT that residual and is closed — `globalThis["Resp" + "onse"]` folds (S354); see the sibling case `protect-raw-egress-computed-response`.
rationale: §14.8.9 closed-world precondition (SPEC.md:8519-8525): an egress path the compiler cannot analyze — including 'a manual `Response` / `handle()` body (§40)' — carrying a protected-origin column SHALL fail closed with E-PROTECT-004. The SHALL is on the CONSTRUCT, not on a spelling, so a detector keyed to one surface form under-enforces the normative rule. The leak is real rather than theoretical because the emitted handler's `instanceof Response` passthrough (§12.5) deliberately returns a manual Response BEFORE `_scrml_protect_redact` runs — so a manual Response that the gate misses is never redacted by anything. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-029 Q1).
